activeGoal.title: Build Lean Mass
activeGoal.destination: Build 10 lb of lean mass by October 31, 2026
activeGoal.confidenceThesis: You are more than halfway to the 10 lb lean-mass goal. The build plan is clearly working. There is enough time to finish ahead of schedule if this level of progress continues.
activeGoal.confidenceProvenance: As of the Sep 23 Midweek Briefing
activeGoal.phasePurpose: Build meaningful lean mass from the newly established maintenance baseline while protecting body composition.

guardrail.title: Maintain approximately 8–9% body fat
guardrail.interpretation: Inside the range, so the guardrail is not limiting the build.

training.summary: 15 of 23 comparable movements are improving, led by lower body, upper body and arms. Single-Leg Leg Press is down.
highlights: Leg Press High And Narrow Feet · +67.2%

turningPoints.title: Goal baseline DEXA
turningPoints.body: The starting point every later scan is measured against.

turningPoints.title: Establish Maintenance completed · Lean Mass Build began
turningPoints.body: Establish Maintenance was completed and Lean Mass Build began. The Aug 15 DEXA showed +0.8 lb of lean mass from the baseline.

turningPoints.title: Past halfway to the lean-mass target
turningPoints.body: Lean mass rose 5.0 lb in the month since the Aug 15 scan, and body fat moved into the guardrail range.

coach.whatToDo: Keep executing consistently. Keep the current setup in place.
coach.whatToWatch: Treat the calorie estimate as directional: calorie totals come from logged meals rather than a confirmed full-day total, active calories are a wearable estimate, and food and activity were both recorded on 2 of 3 days. Keep calorie targets where they are unless something more than the estimate calls for a change. The next DEXA will show whether this kind of progress continues while body fat stays in a good place.

completedGoal.title: Visible Abs at Rest
completedGoal.recap: This journey began with a clear finish line: reveal visible abdominal definition without sacrificing the muscle built before the cut. Across eight deliberate weeks, body fat moved from 13.6% to 7.7%, the waist and midsection became substantially leaner, and training continued to protect the shape underneath. The final DEXA and relaxed photos told the same story—the goal had reached its intended conclusion.

highlights.title: The measured starting point
highlights.body: 13.6% body fat established the journey baseline.

highlights.title: Definition became measurable
highlights.body: DEXA reached 10.7% body fat as upper-ab definition and waist separation became increasingly visible.

highlights.title: The finish line aligned
highlights.body: The final DEXA reached 7.7% body fat and the relaxed photo confirmed visible abdominal definition at rest.

highlights.title: Lean mass largely preserved
highlights.body: The journey finished with 147.5 lb of measured lean mass—within the established preservation tolerance.

completedGoal.finalNarrative: This scan represents the successful conclusion of the cut because the numerical target and the final visual confirmation converged: fat mass fell meaningfully, abdominal definition was visible at rest, and measured lean mass remained within the journey’s preservation tolerance.
achievedBy: Lean mass largely preserved through the cut.
Nutrition consistency maintained through the finish.
Training performance remained strong enough to protect muscularity.
completedGoal.unlocked: Reaching 7.7% body fat while largely preserving lean mass created an excellent foundation for the next Build Lean Mass journey.
